rows.description: My mum's new partner tries to be friendly and I refuse. I fear he will replace my dad. It is fine to go slowly. I stay polite, be honest about feelings, and let trust grow without being forced to love.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, fear, grief, guilt, hope
related mind states: affection, fear, resentment, trust

rows.description: My younger brother used my sketchbook without asking, and I shout. My anger is fair, since my things are mine. Wise: tell him calmly, ask a parent to set a rule, and lock away precious things. Hitting or breaking his toy solves nothing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, dependence, favouritism, forgiveness, guilt, protectiveness

rows.description: I get told to share because he is younger, and I feel the rules are unfair. It is fair to ask parents to treat us fairly. Silent grudges grow; I explain what is not okay to lend, and what I can share.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, dependence, favouritism, forgiveness, guilt

rows.description: My elder sister is upset that I broke her pen. I feel bad and hide it. Better to admit it, say sorry, and offer to replace it or help. Lying makes her trust me less.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, dependence, favouritism, forgiveness, protectiveness

rows.description: I feel my parents love my sibling more because they give them more attention. Often it is different needs, not less love. I ask for one-to-one time and say what I feel, rather than trying to become the trouble child.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, dependence, forgiveness, guilt, protectiveness

rows.description: We fight all day and then build a fort together at night. Siblings mix love and irritation. Wise: apologise quickly and remember the fun. Fights do not cancel the bond, but insults can leave marks.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, dependence, favouritism, forgiveness, guilt, protectiveness
related mind states: playfulness, affection, anger

rows.description: I may tease my sister myself, but when a kid outside pushes her, I stand up for her. Siblings are often each other's first team. I defend, then tell a parent, and I do not turn to violence.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, dependence, favouritism, forgiveness, guilt

rows.description: My mother scolds me without hearing both sides, and it feels unfair. I want to say what happened calmly. Wise parents ask each child. Kids who feel unheard grow angrier at each other, not less.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, dependence, favouritism, forgiveness, guilt

rows.description: I run to Mummy every time my brother does something, hoping he gets punished. Sometimes telling is right, but constant tattling damages trust. I try to solve small things myself and tell adults only for real harm.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, dependence, favouritism, forgiveness, guilt

rows.description: My little sister follows me everywhere and touches my stuff. It irritates me, but she looks up to me. A wise older sibling sets kind limits: this is mine, but we can play together at five.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, favouritism, forgiveness, guilt, protectiveness
